title: Agentic Systems Engineer (Digital Services)
description:
About us

At Cambridge Consultants, we believe the future of technology isn't just smart, it has agency. We're moving past passive tools and building human-centred digital services and products: systems that reason, plan, and act around the people who use them. Our work spans autonomous systems at the frontier of biology, sensing, and AI.

We hire self-motivated builders, not ticket-takers. If you thrive in highly agile environments, can cut through ambiguity with first-principles thinking, and want to ship things that matter, this is the kind of place where you'll feel at home.

About the role

You'll be working on systems that haven't existed before. Think of an Agentic Coach that navigates the unpredictability of human biology, or the software architecture behind a fully automated Dark Lab. These aren't chatbots waiting for questions. They're proactive systems that maintain world models, interpret human intent, and intervene before the user knows to ask. These systems create genuine impact for clients tackling problems no one else can solve.

Building them means designing and wiring agent harnesses: layered architectures that span from sensor-edge reasoning to high-level planning, backed by stateful multi-turn reasoning, persistent per-user memory, and robust evaluation pipelines.

You'll work in two directions at once. Internally, you'll use the latest AI tools to sharpen how we build, prototype, and ship. Externally, you'll deliver the breakthrough systems our clients deploy, designed to move from prototype to production at pace.

There's no single technology stack. You'll work with agents, multi-agent systems, and the latest generative AI tools, but your work will always be grounded in solid software engineering. Expect to build scalable distributed systems in core languages l

title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer
locationText: France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Sweden, United Kingdom
description:
Runware is building high-performance infrastructure and products to power the worlds intelligence. Our platform enables developers and businesses to run fast, scalable inference across image, video and emerging modalities, while our Serverless platform allows customers to deploy and scale their own AI models on production-grade GPU infrastructure.
As a Site Reliability Engineer at Runware , you will help ensure these systems remain reliable, performant and resilient as we scale. This is a highly technical, hands-on role working across software, infrastructure and production operations to improve observability, reduce incidents, eliminate operational toil and build lasting improvements across complex distributed systems.
What you’ll do

• Own and improve the reliability, availability and performance of critical production services across the Runware platform

• Define and evolve our reliability practices, including SLIs, SLOs, alerting, observability and production-readiness standards

• Investigate complex production issues across distributed systems, APIs, networking, queues, databases and GPU-backed workloads, participating in our engineering on-call rotation

• Lead and contribute to incident reviews and RCAs, turning recurring failure modes into lasting engineering improvements

• Reduce operational toil through automation, automated remediation and improvements to deployment safety, recovery and system resilience

• Work closely with Engineering and DevOps teams on capacity planning, performance, scaling and architectural improvements as the platform grows

Requirements

• Have strong experience operating and troubleshooting production systems at scale in an SRE, Production Engineering, Platform Engineering or similar role

• Have a strong understanding of distributed systems and are comfortable debugging across applications, databases, queues, containers, networking and infrastructure

• Have experience designing and operating observability systems using metrics, logs and distributed tracing

• Understand SRE principles including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, capacity planning, incident management and reducing operational toil

• Have experience with Kubernetes, containers, IaC and automated deployment practices, alongside the ability to write software and automation using languages such as Python, Go or PHP

• Take strong ownership of production problems and are comfortable participating in an engineering on-call rotation, taking issues from initial investigation through to long-term remediation

Bonus

• Experience operating high-throughput or low-latency APIs and distributed systems

• Experience with bare-metal infrastructure, GPU environments or AI and ML workloads

• Experience with RabbitMQ or other distributed messaging and queueing systems

• Experience operating MySQL, Redis, ClickHouse or similar production data systems

• Experience with global traffic management, load balancing, CDN platforms and hybrid infrastructure environments

• Experience building automated scaling, capacity management or self-healing systems

Benefits
We’re a remote-first collective, meeting in person twice a year to plan, brainstorm, celebrate wins, and enjoy some face-to-face time. We have core hours for cooperative working and calls, but outside of that your calendar is yours. Work the hours that let you perform at your peak while also building a healthy life.
Our release cycles are fast and intense, but they’re followed by real downtime. After big pushes we expect the team to unplug, recharge, and come back ready & stronger than ever for the next leap.

Generous paid time off - vacation, sick days, public holidays

Meaningful stock options - share in the upside you create

title: Design Team Lead - Ecommerce Marketing Agency
description:
The Design Team Lead runs the day to day work of our Design Team. There are two sides to it. One is craft, which means keeping the standard of the design work high across every client we serve. The other is people, which means keeping the team organised, supported, and able to do good work without getting stuck.

Most of what the team produces is email and SMS campaign design for ecommerce brands, along with ad images, GIFs, short video edits, and the occasional landing page. You will still design yourself, but the larger part of the job is making sure what goes out is right. You are the person who spots what is not working in a design before the client does, and who explains the fix in a way a designer can act on straight away.

You will work closely with Account Managers, who assign the day to day tasks, and with the designers who carry them out. A good deal of the role sits between those two groups: helping an Account Manager work out what a campaign actually needs, turning that into clear direction for a designer, and saying so when a request does not make sense.

The Design Team Lead reports to the Service Director, and works closely with the other departments at Hustler Marketing to make sure design work is delivered well and on time.
About the Role:Mission statement:
To keep the quality of our design work at a level clients notice, and to run a team that is organised, well briefed, and heard.
The first half of that is craft. Reviewing work, spotting what is weak in a design, and giving direction that makes it better. The second half is people. Distributing the week, reorganising it when something changes, and making sure the team's ideas and concerns reach someone who can act on them. We already have a strong team here, independent and reliable. What they need from a lead is someone who listens properly and comes back with a real answer.

General Responsibilities:
Design quality and direction

• Reviewing the team's design work before it reaches Account Managers or clients, and giving feedback specific enough to act on

• Diagnosing why a design is not working, whether that is hierarchy, contrast, the weight of the call to action, the balance of image to text, or how it holds up on mobile, and writing the fix down clearly

• Advising Account Managers on what a campaign needs visually, and pushing back when a brief is thin or a request will not serve the client

• Designing directly when the workload calls for it. This is a hands-on role, not a purely supervisory one

• Keeping the work consistent across a wide range of client brands, niches, and visual identities

• Setting and holding the design standards for email and SMS campaigns, ad images, GIFs, and short video assets

• Understanding each client's visual brand identity well enough to advise on ideas, improvements, and optimisations

Running the week

• Distributing and organising the team's workload week by week, working from the tasks Account Managers assign

• Reorganising the queue quickly when priorities change, someone is unavailable, or a client adds something at the last minute

• Keeping track of who is overloaded and who is not, and rebalancing before it turns into a missed deadline

• Being the first person the Design Team comes to when something is blocking their work

• Making sure the design targets set for each client account are met

The team

• Running the Design Team's group calls and regular one-to-ones

• Collecting the team's suggestions and concerns, taking them seriously, and coming back with an answer, including when the answer is no

• Mentoring designers and helping the less experienced members build their skills

• Onboarding new designers into how we work

• Connecting Design with the other service teams through workshops, short tutorials, and written documentation

• Running training and skill-building sessions for the Design Team

Process and improvement

• Noticing where a workflow, a handoff, or a piece of communication is costing t

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
description:
Join Runware as a Senior Machine Learning Engineer and be at the forefront of developing innovative AI solutions across various media modalities including text, image, video, 3D, and audio. We're building a powerful AI media creation platform designed to revolutionize how content is generated.
As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll take the lead on critical projects, guiding the end-to-end lifecycle from research and experimentation to production deployment and performance monitoring. Your work will help shape the capabilities of our platform and enhance the experiences of users who rely on our cutting-edge AI technologies.
What You'll Be Doing

• Integrate open-source and third-party models into our inference platform

• Lead fine-tuning initiatives (LoRA, adapters, PEFT, domain adaptation)

• Optimise inference workloads for latency, batching, memory efficiency, and throughput

• Benchmark model quality vs cost vs performance across modalities

• Improve inference startup times and stability under high load

• Build evaluation frameworks and internal tooling for model validation

• Work closely with Infrastructure and Backend teams on scalable serving systems

• Monitor production performance and drive continuous optimisation

• Mentor engineers and help raise the ML engineering bar across the team

Requirements
What We’re Looking For

• Deep, hands-on expertise in Python and PyTorch, comfortable working at a level well beyond standard framework usage, including the quirks and edge cases that come with pushing Python for ML workloads

• Demonstrated experience building ML applications and models yourself, not just running or deploying existing ones (e.g. serving a pre-built model via vLLM doesn't qualify on its own)

• Hands-on experience writing GPU kernels in CUDA/C++, or in Triton

• Low-level experience with model internals e.g. working directly with diffusion model architectures (diffusers or equivalent), not just calling high-level APIs

• Experience with the PyTorch compiler (torch.compile) or comparable low-level PyTorch tooling

• Practical experience fine-tuning large models as a repeatable service (LoRA, PEFT, adapters), built for speed and reuse across many models, not a single one-off training run

• Real, verifiable project history e.g. GitHub repos, demonstrating what you have personally wrote

• High ownership and comfort operating in a fast-paced startup environment

Nice to have

• Experience optimizing inference workloads in GPU environments

• Experience with vLLM or custom inference servers

• Experience with diffusion models, LLMs, or multimodal architectures more broadly

• Experience with Kubernetes, Docker, or containerised ML workloads

• Experience building internal ML tooling or developer-facing APIs

• Experience working in high-throughput distributed systems

• Background in AI media generation (image, video, audio)

Benefits
We’re a remote-first team that comes together in person twice a year to plan, collaborate, and celebrate wins. Day to day we keep a few core hours for teamwork, but outside of that you set the schedule that helps you do your best work.
Our environment is fast-moving and ambitious. Big pushes are part of building category-defining products, but we balance that with flexible working, generous time off, and regular retreats so the team can stay sharp and motivated.

title: Manager, Clinical Study Operations
description:
Beacon Biosignals is transforming precision medicine for the brain, from clinical development to clinical care. For Life Sciences partners, we offer the leading at-home EEG platform for clinical development of novel therapeutics for neurological, psychiatric, and sleep disorders. Our Diagnostics business is building the most comprehensive at-home platform for precision diagnostics, combining EEG and cardiopulmonary signals to deliver reimbursable assessments for sleep and central nervous system disorders. Together, we're changing the way patients are diagnosed and treated for any disorder that affects brain physiology.

Beacon Biosignals is seeking a Manager, Clinical Study Operations to lead a team within our Clinical Study Operations (ClinOps) group. ClinOps is responsible for the end-to-end execution of Beacon's internal and external device-based clinical trials - from feasibility and site start-up through recruitment, enrollment, data collection, monitoring, and close-out.

In this role, you will manage a group of direct reports across Clinical Study Operations, overseeing the ClinOps activities on the studies they run - from feasibility and site start-up through data collection, monitoring, and close-out. You will set clear expectations, coach day-to-day execution, escalate risks to leadership before they become problems, and step in directly when a study needs it. Beyond study oversight, you will personally own and drive domain-level ClinOps goals and initiatives - process standardization, tooling, data quality - end to end. You will also represent ClinOps ahead of study execution - in BD conversations, feasibility discussions, and Investigator Meetings - and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Life Science, and BD to keep trials on track and compliant. This role reports to the Director, Clinical Study Operations.

You are expected to bring hands-on clinical trial operations experience - enough to guide your direct reports through site and vendor issues, coach sound day-to-day tradeoffs, and step in directly on complex or high-stakes situations when needed.

At Beacon, cultural and scientific impact comes from people who lead by example. We look for colleagues whose work reflects curiosity, sound judgment, a bias toward simplicity, a self-service mindset, and deep empathy for teammates, stakeholders, sites, and patients. We believe diverse teams build more robust systems and achieve higher impact.
Beacon's asynchronous work practices support a strong remote experience, with in-person hubs in Boston, New York, and Paris. The Clinical Study Operations group is distributed across American and European time zones.

What success looks like

• Support onboarding, and ramp-up for your team as it grows.

• Translate Beacon's strategic priorities into a roadmap for your area - sequencing initiatives, process investment, and team growth - and communicate it clearly to your manager and other stakeholders.

• Oversee ClinOps execution across the studies your direct reports run - feasibility, site start-up, enrollment, monitoring, close-out - and escalate risks and blockers to leadership early, with a clear read on tradeoffs and options.

• Own ClinOps KPIs and goals for your area (execution timelines, enrollment and data quality metrics…), track progress in Asana, and report clearly to leadership and cross-functional partners.

• Exercise sound judgment on issue classification and escalation - including complaint vs. technical-issue calls and device reconciliation/invoicing decisions - stepping in as the escalation point when your reports are uncertain how to proceed.

• Lead domain-level ClinOps initiatives end to end - e.g., process standardization, tooling rollouts, dashboard/reporting improvements - scoping the work, driving it with Engineering, Product, and Data Science partners, and owning the outcome yourself.

Company Overview
Where metal meets momentum. Where bold ideas become the products everyone else wishes they built.
Welcome to JR Metal Works . One of the fastest-rising names in American manufacturing.
We combine precision engineering, modern fabrication technology, and true craftsmanship to create products built to last. As we continue to grow, we remain deeply committed to quality, safety, and continuous improvement, on the shop floor and beyond.

Position Summary
This role is responsible for preparing accurate and timely quotations for sheet metal fabrication projects by reviewing customer drawings, specifications, and requirements. The ideal candidate has a strong understanding of sheet metal manufacturing processes, fabrication methods, material selection, and production routing to develop competitive and profitable quotes.
Job Responsibilities
· Reviewing customer drawings, prints, specifications, and RFQs.

· Ensure quotes are completed by JR Metal Works standards and within customer deadlines.

Qualifications
· Minimum of 3 years of experience in sheet metal fabrication estimating, quoting, manufacturing engineering, or a similar role.
· Strong knowledge of sheet metal fabrication processes.
· Ability to interpret engineering drawings and GD&T.
· Understanding of manufacturing process times and labor standards.
· Strong analytical skills.
· Excellent attention to detail.
· Self-motivated with the ability to work independently in a remote environment.
· Proficiency in Microsoft software.

title: Founding Mobile Developer

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.

The Engineering team builds the systems and products that power SentiLink’s fraud detection capabilities. For this role, you’ll work closely with the NOVA squad across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Fraud Intelligence, and Sales to bring mobile device intelligence into SentiLink’s products and deepen our understanding of the mobile device landscape.

We’re looking for a Founding Mobile Developer with deep systems-level expertise across both iOS and Android. You will own the technical approach and implementation of mobile SDKs and help establish SentiLink’s mobile engineering capabilities. Success in this role means independently navigating ambiguous technical problems, understanding how mobile platforms behave below the application layer, and building reliable mobile capabilities that strengthen our products and fraud detection models.

Over time, your work may also help enable a mobile-optimized experience for SentiLink’s dashboard.

This is a remote, US-based role.

- Own the design and implementation of SentiLink’s mobile SDKs across native iOS and Android.

- Develop a deep technical understanding of device behavior and the signals and capabilities available across both mobile platforms, including networking and other system-level functionality.

- Evaluate technical approaches and make decisions that balance reliability, platform constraints, performance, and maintainability.

- Partner with Product and Engineering to define and deliver mobile capabilities for NOVA.

- Collaborate with Data Science to make relevant mobile device signals and capabilities available for fraud detection models.

- Investigate ambiguous mobile engineering problems independently, using rigorous analysis and experimentation to determine the right technical approach.

- Contribute mobile expertise and technical direction as SentiLink evaluates longer-term opportunities for mobile product

À propos de Lexroom
Chez Lexroom, nous développons l'état de l'art de la recherche juridique agentique. Notre plateforme décompose chaque question juridique en sous-questions précises, puis mobilise des agents spécialisés pour explorer en parallèle les codes, jurisprudences, doctrines et textes européens. Chaque source est minutieusement analysée, les liens implicites entre principes sont identifiés, et toutes les informations sont synthétisées dans un rapport structuré, avec chaque affirmation soigneusement sourcée. Ce qui, auparavant, demandait une semaine à une équipe se réalise désormais pendant une pause café.

Notre mission : rendre le droit plus rapide, plus clair et plus fiable, afin que les avocats et les directions juridiques puissent se concentrer sur l'essentiel.

Nous construisons l'équipe commerciale en France, et nous cherchons la personne qui va structurer et faire grandir l'équipe d'Account Executives.

Pourquoi rejoindre Lexroom ?

- Un produit qui tient ses promesses : nos démos sont impactantes et convainquent dès la première session, pas besoin de six mois de POC.

- Un marché en pleine effervescence : tous les cabinets français recherchent une solution IA, et les usages sont encore à inventer.

- Un avantage concurrentiel fort : vous ne vendez pas un assistant IA de plus, mais une approche radicalement nouvelle que les prospects n'ont jamais vue.

- Un vrai rôle de bâtisseur : vous définissez les standards, les process et la culture commerciale de l'équipe dès le départ.

Vos responsabilités

- Piloter le revenu outbound SMB : objectifs d'ARR, couverture de pipeline, taux de conversion, durée de cycle, ACV, gestion rigoureuse des remises, prévisions fiables.

- Manager et coacher une équipe d'AE full-cycle : 1:1 hebdomadaires, revues de pipeline, coaching sur les appels, stratégie de deals, plans d'amélioration concrets.

- Construire la machine outbound : segmentation ICP, découpage des territoires, stratégie de sourcing des comptes, prospection multicanale (téléphone, email, LinkedIn), standards de cadence et suivi activité → résultats.

- Recruter, onboarder et faire monter en compétence les AE, avec un plan de ramp-up et des jalons clairs.

- Gérer la performance : attentes claires, rituels hebdomadaires (WBR), diagnostic des causes (compétence, motivation, territoire, message) et action rapide en cas de sous-performance.

- Collaborer avec le Marketing (campagnes, contenus, événements), les Partenariats (canaux locaux, KOLs) et le Produit (remontée des insights terrain).

- Garantir la discipline process et outils : CRM irréprochable, séquences rigoureuses, reporting fiable. Les faits avant les impressions.

Profil recherché

- Expérience confirmée en management commercial outbound SMB dans le SaaS B2B, avec une équipe d'AE full-cycle atteignant régulièrement ses objectifs.

title: Tech Lead - Remote Assist, Robotaxi
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Robotaxi Teams

The Robotaxi team is building the capabilities that take Wayve's AI Driver from assisted to fully driver-out operation. Remote Assistance sits at the heart of this effort, the real-time bridge between the vehicle's autonomy stack and human operators that lets us safely handle the moments the AI Driver can't resolve alone. This team owns the end-to-end architecture connecting onboard vehicle systems, offboard services, and operator tooling, balancing latency, reliability, and safety at every step.

🧠 Your day-to-day

- Own the architecture and technical roadmap for Remote Assistance across onboard integration, offboard services, and operator tooling/HMI

- Define and drive the vehicle-operator "contract" - covering data, authority bounds, fallback/MRM behaviour, and failure handling

- Lead cross-team execution across autonomy, safety, platform/infra, and product partners, turning architecture into deliverable workstreams

- Set system-level quality bars for safety-critical RA operation - latency budgets, reliability targets, monitoring, replay/evidence, and incident learning loops

- Act as the technical interface to engineering leadership and safety stakeholders, shaping how Remote Assistance feeds into Wayve's evolving L4 safety case

🧩 What you'll be working on:

- The end-to-end Remote Assistance system onboard vehicle integration, offboard services, and the operator-facing HMI, designed to evolve as one connected system

- Low-latency telemetry and video streaming between vehicle and operator, with hard constraints on glass-to-glass latency and data freshness

- Fallback and minimal risk manoeuvre (MRM) design - the failure-handling logic that keeps operation safe when things don't go to plan

- Decomposing a cross-org architecture into concrete workstreams, some delivered directly and others placed on autonomy, safety, infra, and platform teams' roadmaps

- Building Remote Assistance's contribution to Wayve's L4 safety case, working closely with the safety organisation

👤 You should apply if:

- You have staff-level experience building and owning real-time, safety-critical systems in AV/robotics, teleoperation, aerospace/avionics, industrial control, medical devices, or a comparable domain

- You bring a strong product and customer orientation, and can connect technical performance metrics to rider experience and launch readiness

- You've led cross-org technical roadmaps and landed work across multiple teams you didn't directly manage through architecture, alignment, and execution

- You have deep hands-on expertise in at least one of: low-latency video/telemetry streaming, robotics/AV system integration, control systems, or human-in-the-loop system design

- You have strong safety-first engineering instincts, failure-mode thinking, fallback/MRM design, operational constraint enforcement, and evidence-driven decision making

- You have direct experience with teleoperation, remote driving, or remote assistance systems, including operator UX and authority boundaries

- You're comfortable scaling production systems in ambiguous, fast-moving environments, from prototype through to operational reliability

🌱 Not ticking every box? That's totally okay! If you're passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:

🚗 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules

NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now.
We are currently seeking a The IoT / Edge Architect to join our team in Bethesda (REMOTE), Maryland (US-MD), United States (US).
Job Summary:
The IoT / Edge Architect will serve as the technical lead for the design, integration, and management of secure, scalable IoT and edge computing solutions supporting the client. This role is responsible for architecting the ingestion, processing, and secure management of dosimeter and sensor data from distributed edge devices through AWS GovCloud, ensuring compliance with DoD Impact Level 4 (IL4) and FedRAMP requirements. The architect will collaborate with cross-functional teams-including cloud, cybersecurity, DevSecOps, and stakeholders-to deliver resilient, compliant, and high-performing IoT solutions that support mission-critical and safety objectives.
Job Duties:

• IoT/Edge Solution Architecture: Lead the technical strategy and design for inheriting, integrating, and modernizing client’s IoT-based radiation exposure tracking environment. Define requirements for data ingestion, modeling, system interoperability, and secure device management.

• Cloud Integration & Compliance: Architect and oversee AWS GovCloud landing zone setup, ensuring government compliance, secure network segmentation, and adherence to DoD CC SRG IL4 standards. Define and enforce cloud security configurations, policies, and audit requirements.

• Device Management & Security: Implement secure onboarding, provisioning, and lifecycle management for IoT devices (e.g., dosimeters, gateways) using AWS IoT Device Management, X.509 certificates, and mTLS. Oversee certificate rotation, anomaly detection, and device posture monitoring via AWS IoT Device Defender.

• Data Pipeline & Processing: Design and optimize data flows from edge devices to cloud storage (S3), message queues (SQS), and processing layers (Lambda, Glue, Aurora). Ensure data encryption at rest and in transit, and implement robust ETL pipelines for legacy and real-time data.

• DevSecOps & Automation: Guide DevSecOps teams in automating infrastructure deployment (IaC), compliance checks, and continuous monitoring using AWS-native tools (CloudFormation, Config, CloudWatch, Security Hub).

• Stakeholder Engagement: Serve as the senior technical representative in engagements with stakeholders, Client, and NTT DATA leadership. Communicate architecture decisions, risks, and solution tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Documentation & Knowledge Transfer: Maintain comprehensive architecture documentation, technical artifacts, and processes to enable seamless scaling and knowledge continuity across future task orders

Basic Qualifications:

• Master's level degree in Computer, Electrical or Electronics Engineering or Mathematics with field of concentration in computer science.

• Minimum 10 years of professional engineering experience in distributed systems, embedded software, or edge/IoT architectures, including 5 years in a senior or lead architect role.

• Minimum 3 years of experience applying security controls for IoT/edge systems, including certificate‑based authentication, secure firmware update processes, FIPS‑compliant cryptography, and RBAC/IAM models.

title: Head of Security & Infrastructure
description:
Head of Security & Infrastructure
Location: Remote - United States only (must reside in the U.S.)
Team: Security & Infrastructure
Reports to: CTO (you'll work directly with the CTO)
About Rise
Rise is a global payments and payroll platform built for the way modern teams actually work - across borders, currencies, and rails. We make it possible for companies to pay full-time employees, contractors, and freelancers anywhere in the world, in either fiat or digital assets, with the compliance, tax, and identity infrastructure handled underneath.
Our stack runs on Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Run, BigQuery, Google SecOps), with MySQL , a Node.js / TypeScript application layer, and Cloudflare (including Cloudflare Pages) at the edge. Settlement for stablecoin payments runs on Ethereum and EVM-compatible networks through our own smart contracts and treasury wallets. Because we move money for real people, security and correctness are first-order concerns in everything we ship.
Our Culture
We're a lean, high-trust, high-ownership team. Because we move real money for real people, we hold a high bar for correctness, security, and accountability - the work is meaningful precisely because the stakes are real. We value:

• Ownership over hand-offs. You'll own security and infrastructure end to end and have the autonomy that comes with that.

• Security as a default, not a phase. Handling funds and personal data means security thinking is part of every decision, not a box checked at the end.

• Directness and low ego. We give and receive candid feedback, write things down, and prefer clarity over politics.

• AI-first in how work gets done. We use AI agents and assistants as a core part of daily work - writing and reviewing code and Terraform, triaging alerts, investigating logs, drafting runbooks and policies, and automating the toil that would otherwise eat the day. We expect everyone to work this way and to keep getting better at it.

• Remote-first discipline. We're a globally distributed team spread across time zones around the world, and we communicate asynchronously with a bias toward documentation and reproducibility.

What You'll Do
Working directly with the CTO, you'll own security across Rise's cloud, edge, and on-chain surfaces, and the infrastructure operations that keep production healthy. You are the first dedicated security role at Rise, but you are not starting from zero: you inherit a working program - SOC 2 certification, Google SecOps, Terraform-managed GCP, Cloudflare at the edge, and established on-chain treasury controls - and your job is to own it, harden it, and take it further. Security is the center of gravity for the role, with infrastructure and reliability close behind, on a mostly serverless stack designed to keep operational overhead low.
This is a hands-on leadership role. You will not manage people, but you are the security leader for the company: you set security direction, make the calls on risk, represent Rise to auditors, partners, and customers, and are the person engineering and leadership turn to when a security or infrastructure question needs an answer. It is a builder's seat, not an advisory one - you'll harden what exists, design what's missing, and ship it yourself.
Security operations (SecOps)

• Own and run Rise's security operations: detection engineering, alert triage, investigation, and response across GCP, Cloudflare, GitHub, and Google Workspace.

• Build and tune detections in Google SecOps (Chronicle) over Cloud Audit Logs, load-balancer and Cloud Run request logs, Cloudflare firewall logs, and application telemetry - covering anomalous traffic, abuse, credential misuse, insider risk, and scanning - and keep log ingestion and feed health reliable.

• Establish and track behavioral baselines so new or escalated activity stands out from normal operations.

• Own incident response: detection, containment, forensics, remediation, and blameless post-mortems - and build the tooling and runbook

description:
Knowledge AI Quality Lead | Tripadvisor 

 

About Tripadvisor 

The Tripadvisor Group connects people to experiences worth sharing, and aims to be the world’s most trusted source for travel and experiences. We leverage our brands, technology, and capabilities to connect our global audience with partners through rich content, travel guidance, and two-sided marketplaces for experiences, accommodations, restaurants, and other travel categories. The subsidiaries of Tripadvisor, Inc. (Nasdaq: TRIP), include a portfolio of travel brands and businesses, including Tripadvisor, Viator, and TheFork.

Who are we looking for?
We are seeking a detail-oriented Knowledge AI QA Lead to monitor, test, and evaluate our AI-driven customer experiences to ensure effortless, accurate, and scalable support for all our customers. This role focuses on the end-to-end quality of the customer support journey - from Self-Service and AI-Assist through to Human-Assist transitions. Ideal for a hands-on quality specialist with strong process validation experience, this role bridges customer feedback with technical tuning to continuously improve response accuracy, system compliance, and overall resolution quality.

 

Job Location: Hybrid

This role is a hybrid position that requires 1-2 days per week in our London or Oxford office.

 

What You’ll Do

•
Quality Framework & Testing: Design and execute QA frameworks, test scripts, and evaluation criteria specifically for AI chatbots, automated workflows, and agent copilot tools.

•
Performance Monitoring: Continuously audit and analyze real-time AI conversations and self-service flows to identify intent misclassifications, hallucinations, inaccurate answers, or broken customer journeys.

•
Closed-Loop Quality Feedback: Identify root causes of AI accuracy failures and customer friction; feed actionable insights directly back to AI Automation Leads, Product, and Engineering teams for sprint training and fine-tuning.

Human-Assist QA Integration: Audit the handover from AI to Human-Assist to ensure context retention, CRM integration accuracy, and seamless agent workflow execution.

•
Data Validation & Testing: Conduct pre-release user acceptance testing (UAT) and regression testing for all new AI prompt deployments, KB updates, and workflow releases.

•
Defect & Gap Analysis: Partner with operational teams to identify recurring knowledge base gaps and out-of-scope customer queries to broaden AI coverage safely.

 

Skills & Experience 

Core Qualifications & Experience:

•
QA or Process Improvement specialist with 2+ years of experience in customer contact-center operations or tech support environments.

•
Hands-on experience in testing or auditing AI conversational flows, chatbots, virtual assistants, or automated workflow tooling.

•
Familiarity with process improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma) applied to quality control and operational auditing.

•
Strong understanding of AI behavior, intent structures, and natural language understanding (NLU) failure modes.

•
Proven ability to translate operational customer friction into technical feedback for engineering and product teams.

•
Demonstrated experience in data logging, audit reporting, and root-cause defect analysis.

•
Customer-obsessed mindset with meticulous attention to detail and standard-setting for response quality.

Skills you should bring to the role:

•
Communication: Clear written and verbal reporting skills with the ability to articulate quality defects to technical and non-technical stakeholders (required) .

•
Analytical Mindset: Exceptional eye for detail with the ability to spot subtle pattern failures in data and conversational logs (required) .

•
Data Driven: Comfortable leveraging call

title: Sales Development Representative
description:
As a Sales Development Representative (SDR), you’ll be the first outreach to prospective customers, educating them on how Momence can help grow their business and free up valuable time. This is an inside sales role, focused on cold calling outbound leads, with the goal of booking meetings with prospective customers for our Account Executives. Your quota is based on qualified opportunities produced from your booked meetings. You will:

• Introduce prospective customers to Momence via cold calls (and the occasional email); while there may be occasional work with warm leads, the core focus of this role is cold calling

• Drive lead generation for the sales team by creating qualified opportunities

• Identify influencers and decision makers in an organization

• Manage sales activities, opportunities, and account information in our CRM (Hubspot)

This role supports Momence’s top-of-the-funnel outbound lead qualification. We like to set the expectation that new SDRs will spend about 12 months learning, growing, and contributing to the team in this role before looking to progress to another role within Momence.
You’ve got the sales know-how; we’ve got the Momence know-how. We’ll set you up with the training, information, leadership, and teammate support you need to hone your skills and experience to suit Momence’s unique value proposition and the prospects in our ideal customer profile(s) (ICP). You’ll spend a training-heavy first week getting a sense of the tools, resources, tech stack, and customer info you need to feel ready hitting the phones in week 2, as you gradually begin ramping to full quota attainment.
This is a full time, non-exempt, remote role for which we’re considering qualified candidates who reside in and are authorized to work from any location in the United States.
Working arrangements :
Fully Remote: You can work fully remote within US in this position, provided you have eligible working rights.
About you
You love speaking with people, enjoy tackling tricky problems, and aren’t the least bit skittish about cold calling. You’re hungry to connect with prospects who respond well to empathy, active listening, curiosity, drive, and customer focus. If you’re driven by quota attainment, love helping small business owners out, are a clever problem solver, have at least a year of successful Sales experience, and feel comfortable with Sales fundamentals (think: closing, overcoming objections, driving the conversation, etc.) this could be a great role for you.
What you should have
While we welcome experience from a wide range of career and industry backgrounds, all candidates should meet the following qualifications for consideration:

• 1+ years of sales experience

• Demonstrated capacity for high volume phone work
• Successfully ramped Momence SDRs typically average 160+ outbound dials a day (with the use of a dial-assist tool)

• Disciplined work ethic and eagerness to learn

• Excellent phone presence

• An empathetic, service-oriented, problem solving sales approach

We'll be particularly excited if you also have

• 1+ year of outbound cold-calling experience

• Experience working in early stage startups

• Personal or professional experience in the customer verticals we serve (fitness, yoga, wellness, classes, etc.)

• Experience working, communicating, and connecting with small business owners

At Xplor , we believe that the best innovation and ideas happen at the intersections of our differences - people of diverse cultures, generations, disciplines, and lived experiences. So even if you think you do not tick all the boxes, we still encourage you to apply.
Values and Life at Xplor

Our five core values guide us from how we hire and recognise our team members to how we interact with our customers day to day:

• Find a better way

• Do the right thing

• Say it straight

• Win together

• Own the outcome

title: Senior CRM Manager - Transformation (all genders)
description:
The role

We are looking for a Senior CRM Manager - Transformation to make CRM Self-Service at HelloFresh a reality.

Our central Growth function has a clear vision: Enabling our local marketing and product teams to reach our customers directly, via push notifications, in-app messaging and emails. For this to work in an efficient and customer-centric way, the right guardrails, tools and knowledge need to be in place.

Your first mission is to design, launch and scale our CRM self-service model. You’ll do this hand in hand with our CreativeTech squad (Product and Engineering), who are building the future CRM environment in an AI-native way. You’ll work closely with the squad, and potentially be embedded in it. You’ll be the voice of CRM and of our internal users, helping define what this environment needs to look like so teams can send communications safely and independently.

This is 0-to-1 work in a highly ambiguous space where no one has been before: no playbook, no rules. AI and LLMs change fast and often, so you’ll think about what we need in the future, even if today’s models aren’t ready yet, and be prepared for when they catch up. The learning curve will be steep, but you’ll climb it on the go, together with the team. Our goal: protect our environment from the agents, and protect the agents from our environment. 

From there, your focus will follow where CRM needs it most. You’ll take on further transformation projects, so this role is for someone who enjoys building something new and then moving on to the next challenge.

Above all, we are looking for people who will  make HelloFresh   better.  We believe there are many different ways of developing skills and we love diverse experiences! So even if you don’t “tick all the boxes” but think you’d thrive in this role, we would really like to learn more about you.

What you’ll do

• Lead the self-service rollout: Take end-to-end ownership of the programme, from framing the scope and aligning stakeholders to launching and tracking adoption

• Shape the future CRM platform: Collaborate with Product and Engineering to define how our agentic CRM environment should work, bringing in the needs of users and helping prioritise what gets built next 

• Steer CRM Agents: Build the skills and context agents need to create campaigns reliably, on brand and within our guardrails 

• Build frameworks and playbooks: Develop the documentation, training and processes that let teams send safely without central support

• Enable the teams: Design and run user centric training and onboarding for local marketing and product teams, and turn user feedback into improvements

• Make performance visible: Define and create reportings to measure success

• Scale what works: Identify new use cases to move to self-service and manage each transition end to end

• Drive the next CRM initiatives: Once self-service is established, take ownership of further cross-functional projects that make our CRM team more scalable and efficient

• Modernize processes with AI: Collaborate with the CreativeTech squad and CRM Operations to adapt AI use cases within our CRM workflows 

• Influence the CRM product roadmap: Collaborate with Product and Engineering to shape the future CRM platform, bringing in the needs of users and helping prioritise what gets built next

What you’ll bring

• Strong project or programme management skills, with experience driving complex initiatives across many cross-functional stakeholders, including Tech, Product and local teams

• Experience working in or closely with product and engineering teams, ideally in agile or sprint-based ways of working

• Experience applying AI to real workflows, such as automating processes, creating content or analysing data, and the ability to help non-technical colleagues do the same 

• Solid CRM operations experience (4+ years): you have built and sent campaigns on at least one major CRM platform (ideally Iterable)&nb

title: AI Enablement Engineer
description:
About Phorest
Would you like to create the future of a product used by thousands of businesses and millions of consumers? Phorest Salon Software powers over 11,000 hair and beauty salons in Ireland, UK, Germany, Australia, Finland, USA, Canada, UAE and Netherlands and the platform processes 7 million appointments a month for hair and beauty consumers. Phorest is the number 1 salon software brand for premium independent salons in those markets and our next goal is to become a platform upon which other companies can build applications for premium salons.
Our system touches every point of the salon experience. We have the in-salon software desktop application, Phorest Go (the native staff application), online bookings website for salons, and custom native apps per salon. In a typical month, Phorest processes 3 million appointments and we send over 3 million SMS and 4 million emails. We process 200k online bookings per month and over 150 custom built white label native apps.
The Opportunity
AI is fundamentally changing how software companies operate. At Phorest, we’re investing in AI not just as a product capability, but as a core part of how we work.
We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer - AI Enablement to become a founding member of our AI Enablement team.
This is a highly autonomous hands-on Staff engineering role. You’ll work across Phorest to identify the highest-leverage opportunities, understand how work really happens, and use AI, automation or software to create measurable business impact.
You’ll combine deep technical expertise with strong product judgement, alongside strong commercial and strategic thinking - taking ambiguous problems from discovery through experimentation and into reliable production systems.
The goal isn’t to put AI everywhere. It’s to find where technology can create the greatest leverage, choose the right approach, prove the value it creates, and build the foundations that allow that impact to scale.
What You'll Do

• Set the technical direction for AI Enablement : identify and lead solutions to complex, high-leverage problems across the business and establish the engineering patterns and standards that others can build on.

• Find and deliver the biggest opportunities: work directly with functions to understand their goals and workflows, prioritise where AI Enablement can create the most value, and drive work from problem through to outcome.

• Build the right solution: rapidly prototype and deliver AI-powered tools, agents, automations or conventional software, making pragmatic build-vs-buy decisions based on value, capability, cost, security and maintainability.

• Build production systems teams can depend on: ensure critical solutions are scalable, secure, observable, reliable, maintainable and appropriately owned.

description:

Job Title: Senior Optomechanical Engineer

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"-we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge-on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month-not next year-this is your playground.

Position Summary

- We are hiring a Senior Optomechanical Engineer to own the optics-related subsystems on our robotic weapon platforms: the cameras, thermal imagers, rangefinders, and sensor heads that let our systems find and engage small drones, and the windows, housings, and mounts that keep them working. This role exists because our optics have to hold alignment and image quality on a machine that fires shotguns, slews hard, and lives outdoors in Texas heat, dust, and rain.

- This is not an optical design role. Our lens trains are designed by others, inside and outside the company. Your job is everything that happens to those optics once they leave the designer: how they are held, aligned, sealed, kept clean and dry, protected from shock and vibration, and made to perform the same at 0 °F as they do at 140 °F. You are the person who makes sure we get every bit of performance the optical designer put on paper, and you are the person who tells the designer early when a prescription will not survive the mount it needs.

- The person we want thinks in degrees of freedom. You know where an optic is constrained and where it is free to move, how much it will move with temperature and load, and what that does to focus, boresight, and MTF. You have strong opinions on bonded versus clamped versus flexure mounts, and the experience to back them. You know what Invar, titanium, and stainless buy you over aluminum, and you know when aluminum is the right answer because the error budget allows it and the price does not.

- This is a hands-on role. You will build and align your own assemblies, put them on the shaker and in the thermal chamber, take them to the range, and measure what moved.

Essential Duties

- Own the optical subsystems. Be the responsible engineer for every sensor head, camera module, and optical window on the platform, from concept and requirements through production and field support. Own the optomechanical error budget and the drawings, ICDs, and test procedures that go with it.

- Mount optics properly. Design kinematic, semi-kinematic, flexure, bonded, and retained mounts for lenses, windows, mirrors, filters, and focal plane assemblies. Control preload, bond line thickness, and stress birefringence. Make mounts that can be aligned once and stay aligned.

- Choose materials on purpose. Select housing, cell, spacer, and fastener materials to balance CTE match, stiffness, mass, machinability, corrosion, and cost. Run the athermalization math for focus and boresight, and make the cost-versus-stability call with numbers behind it.

- Manage shock and vibration. Design for weapon recoil, gunfire shock, and gimbal slew loads. Drive structural modes away from excitation, specify or design isolation where it helps, and keep line-of-sight jitter and boresight shift within budget. Run modal and structural FEA and correlate it to test.

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Anduril’s Manufacturing Safety Engineering team partners across Anduril’s manufacturing, engineering, and operations organizations to ensure our production systems are safe to build, test, and sustain at scale. As an engineering discipline, we design safety into the way products are made, covering the equipment, fixtures, test stations, and work instructions on the factory floor, rather than inspecting for it after the fact. Our mandate spans the production lifecycle, from new equipment and line design through ramp and sustained operations. We apply formal risk assessment and the hierarchy of controls to identify hazards early and engineer them out, partnering closely with our Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) experts, controls and manufacturing engineers, and production leadership to keep our people safe while moving at the speed Anduril demands.

ABOUT THE JOB
We are seeking experienced Manufacturing Safety Engineers to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa, CA and engineer safety into how Anduril builds its products. As a Manufacturing Safety Engineer, you will apply formal risk assessment and the hierarchy of controls to production equipment, lift fixtures, test stations, and manufacturing work instructions, identifying hazards early and designing them out in partnership with EHS, manufacturing and controls engineering, and production teams. You will be the on-the-floor technical authority who makes our factories safe without slowing them down, from new equipment and line bring-up through ramp and sustained operations.
This is an evergreen requisition used to build a pipeline of Manufacturing Safety Engineers. This role is based in Costa Mesa, CA, and supports Anduril’s manufacturing operations, including sites at Quonset Point, RI and Atlanta, GA; specific team, site, and program assignments are determined during the interview process based on business need and candidate background.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Lead formal machine and task-based risk assessments on production equipment, fixtures, tooling, and processes, documenting hazards, risk ratings, required controls, and residual risk.

• Review manufacturing work instructions and supporting training material for safety adequacy; author Job Hazard Analyses (JHA) and embed the required controls, PPE, and safe-work steps.

• Engineer and review production equipment such as lift fixtures and material-handling aids in partnership with EHS, and support proof-load testing.

• Assess and design safety into production test equipment.

• Apply the hierarchy of controls and prevention-through-design principles to eliminate or reduce hazards at the equipment and line-design stage.

• Define functional-safety requirements for safety-related control systems and verify their implementation.

• Partner with EHS to ensure engineering controls satisfy applicable OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general-industry requirements (machine guarding, lockout/tagout, electrical, PPE, materials handling).

• Support incident and near-miss investigations and root-cause analysis; drive corrective engineering actions and management of change.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• B.S. Degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Industrial, or Safety Engineering, or equivalent technical d

title: Controller
description:

The Redesign Group is a global technology and cybersecurity Solution Provider leveraging design thinking, interdependent subject matter expertise, and emerging technology solutions to help organizations achieve meaningful transformation. Our globally diverse team members, partnerships with strategic technology manufacturers, and cybersecurity services position us to be a business partner that’s ready for what’s next.

We live by our core values of operating in the service of others, being problem solvers, and focusing on long term partnerships. You’ll excel at Redesign if you thrive in a rewarding environment that moves quickly, challenges you to grow and fosters collaboration. We seek candidates with a hands-on customer-first approach, robust interpersonal and communication skills, strong work ethic and excellent time management. While teamwork is expected, the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment is crucial.

Job Description

The Controller will lead the day-to-day accounting and tax operations - the monthly close, reporting across four legal entities in four countries, revenue and cost accounting, tax and internal controls underneath it all. This role is central to building the financial infrastructure, reporting discipline, and controls needed to support a growing multi-revenue-stream technology and services business.

Reporting to the VP of Finance, you will lead a team spanning general accounting, tax, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and billing - including two direct managers, the Accounting Manager and the Tax Manager. Close, Consolidation & Reporting

• Review and approve the financial statements, reporting package, account reconciliations, and supporting schedules

• Own multi-entity reporting across the US, UK, Canada, and France as a controlled group, including transfer pricing arrangements and foreign currency translation

• Govern the chart of accounts, holding consistent treatment across entities, revenue streams, and cost streams

• Partner with a new FP&A team on the execution of the financial plan -this role owns the actuals and department-level reporting to leaders, with FP&A owning the plan

Revenue & Cost Accounting

• Oversee accounting across the company’s revenue streams: product resale, software subscriptions, maintenance and renewals, cybersecurity, and professional and managed services

• Develop and own the cost allocation methodology used to report gross margin by product and service line, reporting meaningful insights into the profitability of each business unit

• Collaborate with Sales Operations to approve accounting positions on new, non-standard, and judgment-heavy transactions

Tax

• Own the tax function in partnership with the Tax Manager, covering federal, state and local income tax, sales and use tax, VAT, and Canadian indirect tax

• Manage multi-state and multi-country registrations and nexus as the company grows

Systems, Controls & Audit

• Serve as the accounting system owner for QuickBooks, including the integrity of the general ledger

• Partner with Business Systems Developers and Sales Operations to strengthen the Salesforce-to-QuickBooks workflow supporting bookings, billing, and revenue recognition

• Design and maintain internal controls, and prepare the company for its first external audit

• Own sales commission and incentive compensation calculations, accrual methodology, and reporting

• Oversee payroll in partnership with People Operations - payroll accounting and reconciliation across four entities, plus the controls over pay changes, approvals, and off-cycle r

About Us:
Good Business Lab (GBL) is a research-to-action nonprofit that advances access to high-quality jobs for low-income workers. We believe a truly good job is more than wages - it creates conditions for workers to thrive. Yet too few workers have access to sustained wage growth, supportive workplaces, and real opportunities for advancement. GBL works to change this by expanding pathways into better-fit, higher-opportunity work and improving job quality within large employers. We study worker needs, partner with workers and employers to co-design interventions that serve both individual and business goals, and evaluate impact through causal methods. Across manufacturing, retail, and food service, our work shows that improving job quality also improves firm performance. We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

JOIN US IF YOU WANT TO

ABOUT THE ROLE

OUR MODERN DATA STACK

You’ll work with a modern analytics stack centred around SQL, Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran and Claude.

- Strong experience with ELT pipelines and transformation at scale, ideally using dbt.

- Experience with Snowflake or another modern cloud data warehouse.

- Proactiveness in raising areas of data workflows that could be improved and suggesting solutions.

- A collaborative working style and clear communication across technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Comfort using AI tools effectively to move faster, improve quality, and strengthen day-to-day analytical and engineering workflows

INTERVIEW PROCESS

2. Initial chat

3. 30 minute chat with hiring manager

title: Physical Security Lead
description:
About the role

We’re hiring a Regional Physical Security and Safety Operations Lead to help safeguard our people, spaces, and operations every day. individual contributor role with no direct reports , responsible for managing safety and security programs, coordinating vendor services, and driving operational improvements across our offices.

You’ll own core physical security functions, including contract guard operations, access control, surveillance systems, and emergency preparedness. You’ll also serve as a calm, decisive resource during critical incidents, coordinating response efforts with internal partners, building management, and emergency services.

Success in this role requires hands-on execution, sound judgment, and the ability to influence without direct authority. You’ll identify risks, strengthen procedures, and build practical programs that support a safe, secure, and welcoming workplace.

In this role, you can expect to

• Manage day-to-day safety and security operations, coordinating contract guard coverage and holding vendors accountable for service quality, performance, and compliance with post orders.

• Provide operational oversight of the 24/7 Security Support Center (SSC), ensuring consistent monitoring, timely escalation, accurate reporting, and response readiness.

• Coordinate real-time response to security incidents, medical emergencies, and facility issues, engaging appropriate partners and documenting follow-up actions.

• Maintain the reliability of access control, video surveillance, and alarm systems through routine reviews, troubleshooting, and vendor coordination.

• Conduct site assessments to identify vulnerabilities and safety concerns, recommend improvements, and track corrective actions through completion.

• Develop, maintain, and reinforce standard operating procedures, post orders, incident response plans, and emergency protocols.

• Manage relationships with contract security providers and security system vendors, including service reviews and issue resolution.

• Coordinate Emergency Response Team (ERT) recruitment, training, drills, and readiness across office locations.

• Active certification or experience with First Aid, CPR, and AED response standards.

• Partner with Workplace, People, IT, Legal, and other stakeholders to address safety concerns and support employee communications, events, and office operations.

• Review incidents and operational trends to identify recurring issues, improve processes, and measure program effectiveness.

To thrive in this role, you have

• 5+ years of relevant experience in corporate safety and security, physical security operations, military service, law enforcement, or a related field.

• Experience independently owning security programs, coordinating field operations, or managing vendor performance.

• Hands-on experience responding to incidents, exercising sound judgment, and remaining calm under pressure.

• Experience working with access control systems, video management platforms, alarm systems, and incident reporting tools.

• Experience supporting emergency preparedness programs, employee training, and response drills.

• The ability to assess risks, prioritize competing needs, and turn recommendations into practical improvements.

• Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and reinforce standards without direct reporting authority.

• Strong organizational skills and consistent follow-through on documentation, corrective actions, and operational commitments.

• Any security licenses or certifications required for the position and location, and the ability to meet applicable background screening requirements.

• Experience building, leading, or participating in Emergency Response Teams (ERT) within corporate environments.

title: GTM Enablement Manager, Field Training & Readiness - Atlanta
description:
ROLE SUMMARY

Temporal is rapidly scaling its field organization, and setting up every seller to succeed, from day one and well beyond, is critical to meeting and exceeding our most ambitious goals.

As a GTM Enablement Manager, Field Training & Readiness, you’ll be the face of enablement in front of our sales teams. You’ll lead the live sessions where new hires and tenured sellers build the skills and confidence to have great customer conversations: bootcamp modules, workshops, role plays, and ongoing skills sessions. You’ll work from a defined track and a curriculum built with the enablement team, and you’ll bring it to life with your stories, your energy, and your read of the room.

If you’re energized by being in front of a room, believe training should be memorable and behavior-changing rather than a slide-reading exercise, and want to partner closely with the sales and BDR teams on the ground, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Deliver training that sticks. Lead a regular cadence of live, interactive sessions for Account Executives and BDRs and other customer-facing roles, including new hire cohorts, skills workshops, and role plays. Your sessions are built around practice, not presentation.

- Own your delivery track. Take ownership of a defined slate of programs and a delivery calendar. You’ll work from a curriculum built with the broader enablement team and make it your own through storytelling, real examples, and adapting on the fly. You’ll also flag what’s working and what isn’t so the content keeps getting better.

- Partner with the field. Stay close to the sales and BDR teams in Atlanta and beyond. Show up in team meetings, run role-play and call-practice reinforcement with managers, and bring what you hear (what’s resonating, where reps are stuck) back to the enablement team.

- Bring in the experts. You won’t be the expert on everything, and you don’t need to be. You’ll deliver the fundamentals with confidence and know when to pull in an AE, SA, or product expert to take a session deeper.

- Close the loop. Gather feedback and simple leading indicators (participation, skill demonstration, manager input) after every session and use them to iterate.

- Pitch in on the work behind the work. Scheduling, session prep, LMS updates, and content upkeep are shared across the team. You’ll own your share.

- Flex where the impact is. The core of this role is training delivery. As the team and the field grow, there will be room to expand into onboarding, BDR enablement, and broader field readiness.

WHO YOU ARE (NEED TO HAVES)

- Location: Atlanta metro area, or willingness to relocate. This role involves in-person collaboration with our sales and BDR teams, with a strong preference for 1-2 days a week in the office. In-person attendance is required for biweekly bootcamp delivery.

- You’re a natural facilitator. You come alive in front of a room. You’re outgoing, personable, and engaging; you use stories to make concepts real, and you can hold a room’s attention for hours. Your strength is how you facilitate, not just how you present: you read the audience, draw people in, and adapt on the fly. People leave your sessions feeling equipped, not talked at.

- You have a credible foundation in sales or enablement. You come from one of two places: you’ve spent 2+ years in a sales role (AE or BDR/SDR management) and want to move into enablement, or you’ve spent 5+ years delivering sales training or enablement at a comparable company or level. Either way, sellers listen to you because you understand their reality and speak their language.

- You earn credibility with humility. You know you aren’t the expert in our product or our customers. You build trust by being curious, prepared, and honest about what you know, and by bringing the right people into the room when it matters.

- You’re coachable and a team player. You take feedback well, you ask for it, and you improve fast. Enablement touches every part of the business,
